newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prices do not call for policy change -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan prices do not call for policy change -- BOJ.

text.p: Recent movements in prices in Japan do not call for a change in monetary policy, Jun Sekine, the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) director of price statistics told Reuters Financial Television on Friday.

"Prices at the moment are not in the situation where there would be suddenly something to worry about. If you look at the economy at the moment, there is no need to change the current monetary policy at the moment," he said.
Consumer price figures released earlier on Friday showed a 1.2 percent rise for the Tokyo area in April. The increase followed a rise in the sales tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Sekine also said he believed that current interest rates reflected movements in the economy, prices and the yen/dollar rate.

He also said that import prices had been rising, particularly in the autumn to winter period, on the back of an increase in oil prices and a weaker yen, but that this had yet to feed into domestic prices.

He said that, although prices for raw materials were rising, this increase in prices was being absorbed at different stages along the way and it was important to keep a close watch on how long this situation could last.
